history.summary: 354-unit D14 leasehold (1995) at Kembangan, 2BR at $1.31M / $1,519psf, 130m from EW6 Kembangan MRT. URA shows 6.33% over 58 txns and asking is near the $1,392 median, but resident reviews flag serious building defects — roof waterproofing failing, rainwater leaking into units, derelict stacks, and amenities shut for noise complaints. The maintenance overhang outweighs the cheap MRT-adjacent entry.
history.rating_rationale: On paper the location is excellent (130m to Kembangan EW6) and the 6.33% URA looks fine, but multiple reviews describe failing roof waterproofing with water ingress into units, units in derelict condition, and facilities closed indefinitely — classic signs of an under-funded sinking fund and looming special-levy / capex risk on a 31-year-old lease. For a 5-7yr investment that combination (ageing lease + deferred maintenance + likely levies) is a material downside, and it explains a price near median despite a prime MRT location. Investment Avoid; the MRT proximity is its only real merit.
red_flags: Reviews report failing roof waterproofing and rainwater leaking into units
Units in derelict condition; facilities closed indefinitely (noise complaints)
Deferred-maintenance / special-levy risk on a 1995 (~69-yr) lease
Ageing leasehold — financing and appreciation headwinds over the hold
catalysts: 130m to EW6 Kembangan MRT — strong transit (the one positive)
Low $1.31M quantum if a buyer can stomach the capex risk

history.summary: A spacious 1,313 sqft 99LH 3BR right next to Kembangan MRT (130m, 2-min walk) in a 354-unit D14 family estate, at $1,291 psf — ~7% under the $1,392 district median. Doorstep East-West Line access and a sub-$1.7M quantum are strong, but the 1993/1995 vintage (lease ~67yr remaining) and thin 58-txn base are real constraints.
history.rating_rationale: The location is the case: 130m / 2-min to Kembangan MRT on the East-West Line is a true doorstep transit premium that durably supports both rental and resale, in a well-regarded family-friendly D14 enclave (7.7/10 resident rating, spacious layouts). At $1,291 psf it's a ~7% discount to median on a large 1,313 sqft unit, with a friendly sub-$1.7M quantum and 6.3%/yr resale CAGR. The brakes on Strong Buy are age — 99LH from 1993, so only ~66-67 years remaining over the hold, with the financing/CPF caution band approaching — plus a thinner 58-txn liquidity base. For a 5-7yr horizon the MRT-adjacency value outweighs the lease concern, but lease decay is the key resale risk to price in.
red_flags: 1993/1995 vintage — ~66-67yr lease remaining, nearing the <70yr financing/CPF caution threshold over the hold
Thinner liquidity: 58 URA txns and 354-unit base vs 500+ unit peers
Dated facilities relative to newer D14 stock

history.summary: Referee reconciliation: doorstep Kembangan MRT and below-median PSF are real, but building-level defects found in the sibling 2BR evaluation (failing roof waterproofing, water ingress, special-levy risk) apply to every unit type and cap the rating.
history.rating_rationale: Downgraded from Buy: 130m EWL MRT + 7% PSF discount remain, but documented waterproofing failures and dereliction reported in 2BR research are building-wide; add 1995-vintage lease decay and the value case needs a deep defect/levy check before any Buy.
